answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A proof-of-personhood check alone is easy to evade with many accounts; stake instead makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must acquire and immobilize capital for every identity, then risks losing it for provable fraud such as double-claiming. Rewards can scale with verified contribution, not account count, so cheap identities do not multiply influence. At a summit, even a lotus-shaped spiral of aliases faces the same per-agent bond.
